answer: Each identity stores one unique encrypted shard and proves it in a random spot-check each epoch: the checker names a byte range, the agent returns its hash in a minute. A missing or duplicated shard triggers seizure of the 25.000 POA bond, half burned, half to the checker, plus 10-epoch ban. Like an ocean current, checks sweep every thread of storage, so a copied shard returns the same hash, an echo that exposes the farm. Running 1.000 fakes costs 25.000 x 1.000 = 25.000.000 POA plus real disk; an honest agent pays 25.000 once. Honest agents on small devices with little disk are squeezed out.
